text:
maria: Heads-up — perf regression on SM86 nodes after yesterday's runtime tweak. seq_len=128 now picks slow float32 gemm path, not fp16/tc. traces attached.

chris: repro script?

maria: quick repro gist: `./scripts/prof.sh --model llama2 --seq 128 --batch 1 --device sm86`

raj: can you paste profiler snippet? curious which kernel ID.

maria: profiler snippet:
```
[PROFILE] model=llama2 seq=128 batch=1 device=sm86
kernels:
  - matmul_f32_slow (12.3ms)
  - matmul_fp16_tc_fast (2.1ms)
  - attention_kvcache (1.8ms)
decision: picked matmul_f32_slow
```

dana: weird — kernel selector should prefer fp16 tc when SM >= 86 and tensor cores available. selector heuristic might be mis-evaluating `supports_bf16` vs `supports_fp8` flags.

infra-bot: node pool sm86-rt-4 shows driver 535.12, cuda 12.1

chris: recent change was: fallback to generic matmul when sequence gating threshold hit for batching edge-case. maybe gating wrongly triggered at seq=128.

raj: can we test gating table? paste current gating config.

maria: gate config:
```
seqlen_gating:
  - threshold: 64
    preferred_kernel: fp16_tc
  - threshold: 256
    preferred_kernel: f32
```
looks like comparator uses <= instead of <

dana: ahh that's the bug then. <= will push 128 into the higher threshold. change to `<` then run CI perf.

maria: quick patch incoming. also discovered kvcache prefetch path adds 0.6ms unexpectedly when matmul fallback happens.

perfbot: benchmark run queued (job 4821). will post results.

chris: add a guard to require tensorcore availability check (HW + driver) before preferring fp16_tc. sm86+driver>=536 maybe?

raj: note FP8 flags: driver 535 reports fp8 advert false on some nodes; hardware ok but driver exposes false. need driver detect logic.

dana: for safety, add env override `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fp16_tc` to repro in CI.

maria: sounds good. I'll push patch to PR and link here. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2301 :thumbsup:

perfbot: benchmark results: baseline(master) 2.3ms, patched-selector 1.9ms for seq128 on sm86. kvcache hit-rate unchanged.

chris: nice. roll it to canary on sm86 pool and monitor.

infra-bot: canary deployed to pool sm86-canary-2; 4 nodes.

dana: add synthetic load to confirm no tail-latency regression with batching.

maria: will run load test and report in 30m.
